name: Pinto Art Museum
funding: Private museum founded in 2010 to show the collection of physician and patron Dr. Joven Cuanang. Run by the non-profit Silangan Foundation; entry is ticketed.
watch: Complex designed by artist Antonio Leaño.
records_note: The museum site publishes no annual report, accounts, donor list or board; it names only its founder, Dr. Joven Cuanang.

name: MOCA Bangkok
funding: Privately owned by DTAC telecom founder Boonchai Bencharongkul, who built it in 2012 for his collection of over 1,000 works. His son Kanachai runs it; tickets cost THB 250.
watch: Also runs a Four Seasons art space and a Suvarnabhumi airport display.
records_note: The museum site publishes no annual report, accounts, funder list or board; it presents the founder's message and its mission only.

name: Galeri Petronas
funding: Part of PETRONAS, Malaysia's state oil and gas company, which has built the PETRONAS Art Collection since 1993. Nearly two million visitors since 1992.
watch: Left Suria KLCC in July 2026. A preview opened at Ombak KLCC on 21 August 2026; full opening is due by end 2027.
why_flagged: Part of PETRONAS, Malaysia's state oil and gas company, which has built the PETRONAS Art Collection since 1993. Nearly two million visitors since 1992.
records_note: No records of its own: owner PETRONAS posts annual and integrated reports for 2014 to 2025, financial reports, and names its eight directors.

name: Tainan Art Museum
funding: Administrative corporation. 2025 revenue NT$201M: Tainan City subsidy NT$89.7M, Ministry of Culture and others NT$25M, tickets and parking NT$57M, donations NT$3.7M.
watch: Opened 27 January 2019. In 2025 the Ministry of Culture set up a preparatory office for a planned Tainan National Art Museum.
records_note: Publishes annual reports 2019 to 2024, final accounts 2017 to 2025 and yearly donor lists to 2025; names only its chair, not the full board.

name: Red Brick Art Museum
funding: Private museum built by collectors Yan Shijie and Cao Mei, who invested nearly RMB 400 million over eight years.
watch: The 20,000 sq m site was designed by Dong Yugan of Peking University. Yan is described only as a collector and entrepreneur.
records_note: The museum site has visitor, exhibition and research pages only; no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board are published.

name: Galeri Nasional Indonesia
funding: State gallery owned by Indonesia's Culture Ministry, a ministry created under President Prabowo; before that it sat under the education and culture ministry. Holds 1,770 artworks.
watch: On 19 December 2024 it cancelled Yos Suprapto's show ten minutes before opening after he refused to cover more paintings of Jokowi.
why_flagged: State gallery owned by Indonesia's Culture Ministry, a ministry created under President Prabowo; before that it sat under the education and culture ministry. Holds 1,770 artworks.
records_note: Its site could not be reached, so reports, accounts, funders and board were not checked; no gallery report turned up in search.

name: UCCA Center for Contemporary Art
funding: Not-for-profit museum accredited by Beijing, funded by its gala, patrons, corporate sponsors and grants. 2025 partners: Louis Vuitton, Dior, Bloomberg and Aranya; 901,435 visitors.
watch: UCCA cancelled a 2019 Hung Liu show after Beijing denied a permit. In 2022 it pulled a Li Songsong painting after a complaint.
why_flagged: Not-for-profit museum accredited by Beijing, funded by its gala, patrons, corporate sponsors and grants. 2025 partners: Louis Vuitton, Dior, Bloomberg and Aranya; 901,435 visitors.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2024 and 2025, whose 2025 report names partners, and lists about 30 Foundation Council members; no accounts found.

name: West Bund Museum
funding: Run and paid for by the state-owned West Bund Group. The Centre Pompidou partnership was renewed in 2023 for five years. Joint shows since 2019 drew over 2 million visitors.
watch: Local officials had fewer than five works removed from the 2019 opening show, The Shape of Time. Pompidou says it does not self-censor.
why_flagged: Run and paid for by the state-owned West Bund Group. The Centre Pompidou partnership was renewed in 2023 for five years. Joint shows since 2019 drew over 2 million visitors.
records_note: Its site could not be reached, so nothing was checked; the state-owned West Bund Group funds it under a five-year Pompidou partnership.

name: National Visual Arts Gallery
funding: Owned by the Government of Malaysia and run by the National Visual Art Development Board, a statutory body under the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture. Most exhibitions are free.
watch: In February 2020 it removed four works from Ahmad Fuad Osman's retrospective. Nearly 400 artists and 55 collectors petitioned; a deputy minister sought their return.
why_flagged: Owned by the Government of Malaysia and run by the National Visual Art Development Board, a statutory body under the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture. Most exhibitions are free.
records_note: Its site names past main sponsors such as Shell and Petronas on an undated page; reports, accounts and board could not be checked.

name: National Art Museum of China
funding: State museum funded by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism. About 1.05 million visitors in 2016. German collectors Peter and Irene Ludwig donated 117 works.
watch: Opened in 1963; holds over 110,000 works. Jean Nouvel's larger building was announced in 2014; no budget for either was found.
records_note: Its own site is unreachable; an archived copy shows no reports, funders or board, and its ministry publishes final accounts covering it.

name: Shanghai Biennale
funding: Run by the state-owned Power Station of Art; budget undisclosed and paid mainly from Shanghai city government funds. 2025 partners: Aesop, Denza, Langham hotels and lighting maker Flos.
watch: In 2012 officials demanded cuts to Yuri Albert's work, so he withdrew; a committee rejected Barbad Golshiri's proposal. Both artists published their accounts.
why_flagged: Run by the state-owned Power Station of Art; budget undisclosed and paid mainly from Shanghai city government funds. 2025 partners: Aesop, Denza, Langham hotels and lighting maker Flos.
records_note: The organiser's site renders by script and showed no text, so nothing was checked; the budget is undisclosed and mainly city funds per press.

name: Bangkok Kunsthalle
funding: Her husband Soopakij chairs CP Group, Thailand's largest private company.
watch: artn't activists staged a guerrilla protest inside, in shirts reading 'world class exploitation'. CP Group's CP Foods faced 2014 slavery claims in its prawn-feed chain.
why_flagged: Opened January 2024 by philanthropist Marisa Chearavanont through her Khao Yai Art; no sponsors are named. She is married to Soopakij Chearavanont, chairman of CP Group.
records_note: Its site now redirects to a script-built page that showed only headings, so nothing was checked.
